facts: Universal Display lowered its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $630-$670 million from the prior $650-$700 million range, citing reduced near-term visibility and macro pressures.

Q1 2026 revenue was $142 million, down 14% year-over-year from $166 million, while material volumes decreased only ~4%, with the gap driven by customer mix and prior-year tariff-related Chinese purchasing.

The Board authorized a new $400 million share repurchase program after fully utilizing the prior $100 million authorization, during which UDC repurchased ~924,000 shares (including ~633,000 shares for $66 million in Q1).
Q1 net income fell to $36 million ($0.76 per diluted share) from $64 million ($1.35) a year earlier, with operating margin compressing to ~30% from ~42%.
Industry square-meter area growth expectations for 2026 have been cut to roughly 2%, down from the mid-single-digit/~6% assumption underlying prior guidance.
Q1 royalty and licensing fees dropped to $54 million from $74 million year-over-year, while the materials-to-royalty ratio was ~1.5:1 in Q1 versus a full-year expected average closer to 1.3:1.
The company ended Q1 with approximately $911 million in cash and investments and generated $109 million of operating cash flow in the quarter.
Management expects Q2 revenue to be sequentially higher than Q1, with mid-to-high 40% of full-year revenue in the first half and the balance in the second half.

Phosphorescent blue commercialization timelines are being extended as customers pursue varied hybrid (phosphorescent + fluorescent) architectures, though UDC still projects up to a 25% initial OLED panel energy efficiency gain upon adoption.

Major Gen 8.6 OLED capacity expansions remain on track, including Samsung Display's $3.1 billion fab nearing commercial shipments, BOE's $9 billion fab targeting mass production in 2H 2026, Visionox's $7.6 billion facility beginning equipment move-in, and TCL China Star's $4.1 billion plant under construction.
Q4 2025 reported revenues were $4.7 billion with organic constant currency growth of 2%, while system-wide revenue reached $5.1 billion.
Full year 2025 adjusted earnings per share was $2.97, representing a constant currency decrease of 38% year-over-year.
Q4 adjusted EBITA margin was 2.1%, equal to prior year, with SG&A reduced 4% in constant currency while driving organic growth.
The Manpower brand grew 5% in Q4 on organic constant currency basis with 6 consecutive quarters of growth in the U.S., while Experis declined 6% and Talent Solutions declined 4%.
Italy revenue increased 7% on a days adjusted constant currency basis with OUP margin of 6.7%, standing out as a clear outperformer.
France revenue decreased 3% on a days adjusted constant currency basis but showed 4 consecutive months of sequential improvement.
Germany remains a difficult market with revenues declining 22% on a days adjusted constant currency basis in Q4.
Q1 2026 EPS guidance is $0.45 to $0.55 with constant currency revenue guidance of 1% growth at midpoint and EBITA margin projected up 10 basis points year-over-year.
Full year 2025 free cash flow was an outflow of $161 million compared to an inflow of $258 million in the prior year, with net debt at $806 million at year-end.
The company's AI recruiter toolkit scaled to more than 12 markets is delivering a 7% increase in placement rates, and management reaffirmed commitment to 4.5% to 5% EBITA margin target over time.
Cipher has executed 2 data center campus leases representing 600 megawatts of gross capacity and approximately $9.3 billion in contracted revenue, with initial terms of 10 to 15 years.
The company expects its leases to generate $669 million of average annualized net operating income from October 2026 to September 2036, rising to approximately $754 million in annual NOI by 2035.

Cipher completed a $2 billion bond offering at 6.125%, which was 6.5x oversubscribed with approximately $13 billion in orders allocated to over 200 accounts, and included a $233 million CapEx reimbursement of prior equity contributions.
As of December 31, 2025, the company had $754 million of unrestricted liquidity, including $628 million in cash and $125 million in Bitcoin.

Fourth quarter revenue was $60 million, down from Q3, and the company reported a GAAP net loss of $734 million, driven primarily by a $450 million noncash mark-to-market on the embedded derivative liability of the 2031 convertible notes.

The company sold its 340-megawatt joint venture bitcoin mining sites (Alborz, Bear, and Chief) to Canaan in an all-stock transaction and plans to exit its remaining 1,166 Bitcoin position entirely by end of 2026.

Following the sale of JV sites and Black Pearl decommissioning, Cipher's bitcoin mining hash rate will be approximately 11.6 exahash per second, solely from the Odessa site operating at a fixed PPA of approximately $0.028 per kilowatt hour through July 2027.
Approximately 85% of existing infrastructure at Black Pearl is expected to be repurposed for the AWS lease, reducing execution risk and improving capital efficiency.
The company acquired Ulysses, a 200-megawatt site in Ohio with all necessary PJM interconnection approvals expected to energize in 2027, and is in advanced discussions with potential HPC tenants.

Stingray, a 100-megawatt site in Andrews, Texas, is fully interconnection approved and on track to energize in Q4 2025, with the company in advanced lease negotiations with a preferred tenant and expecting lease economics to be among the most favorable achieved to date.
Q1 2026 total revenues were $572 million, up 8% year-over-year, while recurring and other revenue grew 9% year-over-year to $544 million.
GAAP net income was $156 million ($3.04 per diluted share) and non-GAAP net income was $161 million ($3.15 per diluted share) on 51 million diluted shares.
Adjusted EBITDA reached $275 million, expanding 50 basis points year-over-year to a 48.2% margin.

Paycom repurchased approximately 8.4 million shares (about 15% of shares outstanding as of year-end 2025) for $1.06 billion during Q1, and the board approved a new $2 billion buyback authorization on May 4 to replace the prior one.
The company paid approximately $18 million in cash dividends in Q1 and declared a next quarterly dividend of $0.375 per share, payable in early June.
In April, Paycom replaced its revolver with a new 5-year, $2.125 billion credit facility, of which $675 million is currently drawn.

Full-year 2026 guidance was reaffirmed: total revenue of $2.175–$2.195 billion (~6.5% growth at midpoint), recurring and other revenue growth of 7%–8%, and adjusted EBITDA of $950–$970 million (~44% margin at midpoint), including ~$103 million of interest on funds held for clients.
Average daily balance on funds held for clients was approximately $3.1 billion in Q1, up 8% year-over-year, and cash and cash equivalents ended the quarter at $154 million.
IWant AI usage has grown another 33% since the end of Q4 2025, and the tool is included free with the system rather than monetized separately.

Management stated Paycom serves approximately 5% of its addressable market, indicated Q1 bookings came in on budget after a 3-month sales retraining initiative, and noted client revenue retention increased in 2025 with Net Promoter Score continuing to rise.
Q2 FY2026 revenue was $274.1 million, a decline of 3.4% from $283.8 million in the prior year, primarily due to Clear Eyes supply constraints and lower cough/cold category sales.
Adjusted EPS for Q2 was $1.07, slightly below the prior year's $1.09, with lower sales offset by favorable A&M timing and improvements in interest expense and share count.
First half free cash flow was $133.6 million, up approximately 10% versus the prior year, with full year guidance maintained at $245 million or more.
The company repurchased 1.6 million shares for approximately $110 million in the first half, with over 1.1 million shares repurchased opportunistically in Q2 alone.
Full year adjusted EPS guidance was raised to the higher end of the prior range at $4.54 to $4.58, driven by share repurchase efforts.
The strategic acquisition of eye care manufacturer Pillar5 for approximately $100 million is expected to close in Q3, funded primarily with cash on hand.
DenTek dental guards now represents over half of the DenTek brand's revenue with market share exceeding 50% of the category, gaining over 5 percentage points in share versus last year.
First half gross margin of 55.7% was up 60 basis points versus prior year, with full year gross margin expected at 56.5%.

Net debt stood at approximately $900 million at September 30, with a covenant-defined leverage ratio of 2.4x, and the company expects to generate $1 billion or more in cash flow over the next four years.
Q3 FY2026 revenue is expected to be approximately $282 million, down versus prior year due to $5 million of Clear Eyes shipments pulled into Q2 and anticipated e-commerce retailer order adjustments.

Omnicom now expects annual run rate synergies from the IPG acquisition to double from the initial estimate of $750 million to $1.5 billion over the next 30 months, with $900 million expected to be achieved in 2026.

Omnicom's Board authorized a $5 billion share repurchase program, including a $2.5 billion accelerated share repurchase program launched on the day of the call, with an additional $500 million to $1 billion planned for the balance of 2026.

Omnicom identified nonstrategic or underperforming operations with approximately $2.5 billion in annual revenue to sell or exit, and has already completed sales or exits representing annual revenue exceeding $800 million.
The retained portfolio of businesses generated revenue of $23.1 billion for the 12 months ended September 30, 2025, which Omnicom will use as the baseline for forecasting 2026.
Excluding planned dispositions and assets held for sale, organic revenue growth in Q4 2025 would have been approximately 4%.
Adjusted EBITA in Q4 2025 was $929 million with a 16.8% margin, an increase of 10 basis points compared to the prior year.
Omnicom recorded $1.1 billion in severance and repositioning costs, a $543 million loss on planned dispositions, and $187 million in acquisition-related costs in Q4 2025.

Net interest expense is expected to increase by approximately $210 million in 2026 compared to 2025, driven by approximately $125 million from IPG's long-term debt and approximately $50-55 million from bond refinancing and incremental commercial paper borrowings.

Omnicom estimates shares outstanding will decline by approximately 9% to 11% from the December 31, 2025 balance of 313.1 million by end of 2026, with weighted average shares outstanding reduced by approximately 7% to 8%.

Of the $1.5 billion in expected synergies, $1 billion is from labor cost reductions, $240 million from real estate consolidation, and $260 million from G&A, IT, procurement and other operational savings.
Q1 2026 revenue was $20.9 million, flat year-over-year, with management citing severe nationwide weather and power outages in late January and February as headwinds to demand.
Gross profit was $7.4 million with gross margin of 35.5%, down from 36.2% a year ago, and management expects full-year gross margin to trend closer to 36%.
Adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $541,000, an improvement from a $1 million loss in the prior year period.
GAAP net loss from continuing operations was $0.13 per diluted share, adjusted EPS loss from continuing operations was $0.07, and consolidated adjusted EPS was positive $0.01.
The company reaffirmed full-year 2026 revenue guidance of low to mid-single-digit growth compared to 2025.
The transition services agreement with INSPYR concluded on March 31, allowing BGSF to operate as a stand-alone property staffing company starting in Q2 2026.

Management estimates ongoing G&A costs of approximately $12 million annually (including ~$2 million in public company costs), and targeted selling cost actions taken late in Q1 are expected to generate ~$1 million in annualized cash savings, with full benefit realized starting Q3 2026.
BGSF repurchased 170,862 shares at an average price of $5.11, totaling approximately $873,000, and exited the quarter with a debt-free balance sheet.
Income from discontinued operations included a $918,000 cash gain from the final net working capital settlement on the sale of the Professional division.
The newly launched PropTech consulting services via the Yardi partnership could represent approximately 1% to 2% of total revenue in 2026 if execution continues as planned.
Eversource delivered full year 2025 non-GAAP earnings per share of $4.76, compared to $4.57 in 2024, within its revised guidance range of $4.72 to $4.80.

The company announced a new 5-year capital investment plan of $26.5 billion for 2026-2030, a $2.3 billion increase over the prior 5-year plan, with electric distribution being the largest driver of the increase at $696 million.
Eversource projects 2026 EPS guidance in the range of $4.80 to $4.95, with growth described as more moderate due to timing of key regulatory outcomes.
The company expects to deliver earnings growth towards the upper half of its 5% to 7% long-term EPS growth range by 2028, measured off of expected 2027 earnings results.
Eversource's FFO-to-debt ratio improved by more than 400 basis points at Moody's over the last 12 months ending September 30, 2025, and 300 basis points at S&P for 2025.

The 5-year financing plan includes $800 million to $1.1 billion in equity issuances regardless of whether the Aquarion sale closes, with $8.5 billion to $9 billion from incremental debt and alternative financing solutions qualifying for $1.3 billion to $2.5 billion in equity content.

The company still holds roughly $500 million in unused investment tax credits from its tax equity ownership in South Fork Wind, which will help it remain essentially a noncash federal taxpayer for several years.

PURA is expected to issue a final decision on the Aquarion Water sale on March 25 following a court remand, and a storm cost prudency decision is expected in July, enabling securitization proceeds of up to $1.5 billion by Q3 2027.

Eversource filed notice of intent for an Aquarion rate case seeking $88 million in additional revenues and plans to file its first CL&P rate case in approximately 8 years by mid-2026, with rates expected to take effect mid-2027.

The updated capital plan includes an additional $1 billion of potential upside tied to Connecticut AMI deployment not yet in the base plan, with a revised cost estimate and regulatory discussions expected in the near term.

Tradeweb crossed $2 billion in annual revenue for the first time in 2025, marking the 26th consecutive year of record annual revenues and the seventh consecutive year as a public company producing double-digit revenue growth.
Fourth quarter 2025 revenue was a record $521 million, up 12.5% year-over-year on a reported basis and 9.9% on a constant currency basis.
Full year 2025 adjusted EBITDA margin was 54%, expanding 64 basis points year-over-year, with adjusted EPS growth of 19% and free cash flow growth of 32%.

January 2026 reported record volumes and revenues with total revenue growth of 17% year-over-year, and adjusting for one fewer trading day and an $8 million LSEG data timing shift, average daily revenue growth was 26% year-over-year.
The Board approved a new 2026 share repurchase program authorizing up to $500 million, while the company repurchased approximately $157 million of stock in Q4 2025 and January 2026 combined.
Global swaps delivered record quarterly revenues up over 25% year-over-year, with total swaps market share increasing from 20.8% in Q4 2024 to 23.3% in Q4 2025.

U.S. credit revenues fell year-over-year in Q4, with retail corporate credit revenues down nearly 30%, though institutional RFQ average daily volume grew over 10% and RFQ share of overall TRACE achieved a new quarterly record.

Adjusted expense guidance for 2026 ranges between $1.1 billion and $1.16 billion, with the company expecting to drive adjusted EBITDA and operating margin expansion at either end of this range compared to 2025.

The company held approximately $2.1 billion in cash and cash equivalents with free cash flow exceeding $1 billion for the year, and held approximately $1.6 billion of Canton Coins with a fair value of approximately $243 million.

Asian client revenues grew over 35% and European client revenues grew over 25% in 2025, with approximately 42% of Q4 revenues derived from international clients and nearly 50% of revenue growth since the IPO coming from non-rate businesses.
Q3 2025 total revenue of $66.7 million grew 19% year-over-year and was at the high end of guidance.
Aerospace and defense revenue reached a record $45.6 million, up 50% year-over-year, with defense product sales growing 71% year-over-year.
Product gross margin expanded to a record 41% in Q3 2025, up from 28.8% in Q3 2024.
Adjusted EBITDA was $7.1 million in Q3 2025, compared to a loss of approximately $1 million in the same quarter last year.
The company signed a new $50 million contract for an existing long-running missile program incorporating one of its laser sensing products.
Q4 2025 revenue guidance is $72 million to $78 million, with adjusted EBITDA expected to be $6 million to $11 million.
Full year 2025 A&D revenue growth is now expected to exceed the prior outlook of at least 40% year-over-year.
The company ended Q3 with $116 million in total cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash and investments, and was free cash flow positive in the quarter.
The HELSI-2 program, a $171 million contract to develop a 1-megawatt high-energy laser, remains on track for completion in 2026.
Management stated that programs already booked will fill the revenue hole expected when HELSI-2 trails off in the second half of 2026.
Q3 2025 total revenue reached a record $513.7 million, an 8.6% increase year-over-year.
Adjusted EBITDA for Q3 2025 was $56.5 million with margins of 11%, while last 12-month adjusted EBITDA reached $217.1 million.
Innovative Pumping Solutions sales grew 11.9% year-over-year to $100.6 million, while Supply Chain Services declined 5% year-over-year to $63 million.
DXP Water now represents 54% of Innovative Pumping Solutions' year-to-date sales, up from 47% at the same time last year.
On a 9-month comparative basis, native energy IPS backlog is up 56.2% year-over-year, though Q3 saw the first quarterly backlog decline (3.3%) in 10 quarters.
Gross profit margins improved 50 basis points year-over-year to 31.4%, with year-to-date margins up 89 basis points versus last year.
Earnings per diluted share for Q3 2025 was $1.31 versus $1.27 in Q3 2024, with adjusted EPS of $1.34.
Free cash flow for Q3 2025 was $28.2 million versus $24.4 million in Q3 2024, with return on invested capital at 33%.
DXP closed 5 acquisitions year-to-date contributing $74.1 million in sales, and plans to close a minimum of 3 more acquisitions before the end of Q1 2026.
October average daily sales were $7.59 million per day, compared to $8.9 million per day in September and $7.26 million per day in July.
Q3 2025 net sales were $12.6 billion, up 7.2% year-over-year and above the high end of guidance.
Non-GAAP diluted EPS was $0.72, at the high end of guidance despite the ransomware incident impact.
The July ransomware incident's final impact was estimated at 1% to 1.5% of net sales and $0.02 to $0.03 per share.
Client and endpoint solutions grew nearly 13% on an FX-neutral basis in Q3.
IDA (Intelligent Digital Assistant) contributed hundreds of millions of dollars of incremental revenue in Q3.
IDA-driven revenue from non-U.S. operations grew by more than 100% in Q3, and IDA drove quote-to-order conversion rates nearly double those of non-IDA engagements.
Q4 2025 guidance projects net sales of $14 billion to $14.35 billion, representing year-over-year growth of more than 6% at the midpoint.
Q4 2025 non-GAAP diluted EPS is guided at $0.85 to $0.95 per diluted share.
Adjusted free cash flow was an outflow of $110 million in Q3, improved from an outflow of $255 million in the prior fiscal third quarter.
The SMB customer category achieved a third consecutive quarter of sequential growth, with management noting encouraging signs as inflation tempers and interest rates decline.
Q3 2025 revenue grew 6.5% year-over-year in constant currency to $5.4 billion, with all four operating segments delivering organic year-over-year growth.
The company signed 6 large deals each with TCV of $100 million or more in Q3, bringing the year-to-date total to 16, with year-to-date large deal TCV up 40% from the prior year period.
Q3 adjusted operating margin improved 70 basis points year-over-year to 16%, while adjusted EPS of $1.39 grew 11% year-over-year.
On a trailing 12-month basis, revenue per employee rose 8% year-over-year while adjusted operating margin income per employee grew 10%.

Full year revenue guidance was raised to 6% to 6.3% constant currency growth, above prior guidance of 4% to 6%, with full year EPS guidance increased to $5.22 to $5.26 representing 10-11% year-over-year growth.
Approximately 30% of internal code was AI-generated in Q3, with expectations it could reach 50% in the years ahead.
The BPO business grew 10% in the last two quarters and is on track to reach $3 billion in annualized revenue over the next several quarters.
Q3 free cash flow was $1.2 billion, representing 170% of adjusted net income, compared to $791 million a year ago.

The company returned $600 million to shareholders in Q3 through repurchases and dividends, bringing year-to-date returns to approximately $1.5 billion, and remains on track to return $2 billion in 2025.
Fixed price managed services business mix increased from 43% in 2024 to close to 47%, while voluntary attrition declined to 14.5%, down 70 basis points sequentially.

Koppers reported full year 2025 adjusted EBITDA of $256.7 million with a 13.7% adjusted EBITDA margin, the second highest year on record excluding KJCC and a new high watermark on an as-reported basis.

The Catalyst transformation program delivered $46 million in benefits during 2025, and the company now estimates up to $75 million of additional Catalyst benefits over 2026-2028, up from the $40 million previously communicated in November.
Koppers is guiding 2026 adjusted EPS of $4.20 to $5.00 per share compared with $4.07 in 2025, and adjusted EBITDA of $250 million to $270 million.
The company targets $20 million to $40 million in Catalyst benefits achievable in 2026, with the increase primarily driven by manufacturing network optimization.
Performance Chemicals is projecting approximately 11% top-line growth in 2026, driven entirely by market share expansion in both residential and industrial product lines.

If copper markets do not abate as the company enters 2026 contract discussions, current prices (25% higher than 2025 averages) would represent a $50 million pricing pass-through necessary to account for increased copper costs.
Koppers reduced its employee count by 11% from year-end 2024 and 17% from its April 2024 peak, while also cutting adjusted SG&A costs by 15% in 2025.
The company repurchased approximately $38.2 million (nearly 1.3 million shares) in 2025 and has approximately $67 million remaining on its $100 million repurchase authorization.
PC and RUPS now make up 80% of total sales—the highest percentage in company history—closing in on the company's 85% target as part of its portfolio evolution strategy.

Koppers expects 2026 to be an inflection point for cash generation, projecting record operating and free cash flow levels, implying a better than 15% free cash flow yield at the current market cap and targeting $300 million or more in cumulative free cash flow over the next three years.
Q3 orders reached 83.4 million, up 14% year-over-year, driving GTV of $9.17 billion, up 10% year-over-year.
Q3 adjusted EBITDA grew 22% year-over-year to $278 million, while GAAP net income was $144 million, also up 22% year-over-year.
The company increased its share repurchase program by $1.5 billion, bringing total capacity to $1.65 billion, and plans to enter a $250 million accelerated share repurchase program.
Q4 GTV guidance is $9.45 billion to $9.6 billion, representing 9% to 11% year-over-year growth, with orders growth expected to outpace GTV growth.

Q4 advertising and other revenue is expected to grow only 6% to 9% year-over-year due to large brand partners moderating spend amid macro uncertainty, though management is confident in returning to double-digit growth in 2026.
Advertising and other revenue delivered over $1 billion over the past 12 months, with brand partners seeing an average 25% boost in sales when advertising on Instacart.
The enterprise platform now powers more than 350 retailer e-commerce storefronts and more than 240 Carrot Ads partner websites, with 40 net new retailer sites launched in H1 alone.
Over 80% of the company's business is currently nonexclusive, and retailers with enterprise relationships that go nonexclusive continue to show strong growth.
Price parity retailers are growing 10 percentage points faster versus marked-up retailers, driving ongoing conversations with partners about reducing markups.
Large baskets ($75 and above) still represent 75% of the online grocery market, and Instacart maintains 3x higher share of sales than the next largest digital-first player.
Electromed delivered Q1 FY2026 revenue of $16.9 million, a 15.1% year-over-year increase, marking the company's 12th consecutive quarter of year-over-year revenue and profit growth.
Operating income rose 37.8% year-over-year to $2.7 million, representing 15.8% of net revenues compared to 13.2% in the prior year period.
Fully diluted EPS increased 56% to $0.25 from $0.16 in Q1 FY2025, with net income up 44.9% to $2.1 million.
Hospital sales surged 51.7% year-over-year to $1.047 million, while home care distributor revenue grew 41.2% to $829,000.
The direct home care sales force expanded to 57 representatives across 61 territories, with average annualized revenue per rep of $1,052,000, within the target range of $1 million to $1.1 million.
The company has $14.1 million in cash, $24.8 million in accounts receivable, no debt, and working capital of $35.8 million.
The Board authorized a $10 million stock repurchase program, with $1 million of common stock already repurchased in Q1 FY2026.

Of the estimated 923,000 U.S. patients diagnosed with bronchiectasis, only 16% are using high-frequency chest wall oscillation therapy, leaving approximately 800,000 diagnosed patients as an addressable market.

Gross profit margin was 78.1% of net revenues, and management expects to maintain mid-70s or better gross margins given the company's U.S.-based operations with 99% of net revenues generated domestically.
Over one-third of orders are now submitted electronically through the Smart Order e-prescribe solution, enabling faster fulfillment and improved patient outcomes.
Q1 2026 sales were $106.4 million (down 13% YoY), with adjusted EBITDA of $15 million (down 31%) and adjusted basic EPS of $0.15 (down 58%), though all came in ahead of expectations.

Net income was a loss of $134.8 million ($6.30 loss per share) driven by a $179.5 million non-cash goodwill and long-lived asset impairment in Branded Spirits, including ~$27 million for equipment at the Lux Row facility.

The company is temporarily idling its Kentucky distilling operations at Limestone Branch and Lux Row starting in May, affecting 33 employees, while the Lawrenceburg, Indiana facility remains fully operational.
Full year 2026 guidance was reaffirmed: net sales of $480M-$500M, adjusted EBITDA of $90M-$98M, and adjusted basic EPS of $1.50-$1.80.

As a result of the Kentucky idling, expected 2026 operating cash flow improved by $10M to $50M-$55M, free cash flow to $30M-$35M, and peak net leverage was lowered to ~3.5x from prior guidance of 3.75x.
Distilling Solutions sales fell 40% YoY to $28 million and gross profit declined 54% to $8.6 million, with management continuing to view 2026 as the trough year for the segment.
Branded Spirits gross margin expanded 180 basis points to 47.8%, with Premium Plus sales up 1.5% and Penelope Bourbon up 10% YoY, though private label declines weighed on overall segment sales.

Ingredient Solutions sales grew 29% YoY to $34.2 million with gross profit up 56% to $3.8 million (11.2% margin), and full-year segment gross margins were lowered to mid-teens due to higher effluent costs and a planned Q2/Q3 shutdown.

The company discontinued more than 30 tail brands in Q1 with ~15 more planned by year-end, representing ~1% of segment sales but an expected 20 bps annualized gross margin improvement and over $2.5 million in working capital reduction.

Distilling Solutions added more than 20 new customers in Q1 (including a significant national private label whiskey customer) with aged sales up 9%, while the white goods 2026 sales outlook was reduced to up mid-single digits due to commercialization timing.

CMS Energy reported Q1 2026 adjusted EPS of $1.13 and adjusted net income of $346 million, reaffirming full-year 2026 guidance of $3.83-$3.90 per share with continued confidence toward the high end, and reiterating long-term adjusted EPS growth guidance toward the high end of the 6%-8% range.

The Michigan Public Service Commission approved over 65% of CMS's electric rate case ask and maintained a 9.9% electric ROE, while MPSC Staff recommended over 75% of the $240 million gas rate case ask and supported nearly 95% of gas infrastructure investments.

CMS will file its 20-year Integrated Resource Plan in June, including 1.5 GW of new gas capacity to replace retiring units and 13 GW of renewable/clean energy, with a growth scenario flagging upside from data center and manufacturing demand.

Management quantified data center upside at $2-$5 billion of incremental capital per 1 GW of new large load (not in the current plan), with the low end driven by storage plus simple-cycle gas and the high end by combined-cycle gas plus additional substation/wires investment.

Each gigawatt of new data center load materializing in CMS's service territory is expected to reduce average customer rates by approximately 2% annually over a 5-year period, and additional data center investments will not be subsidized by existing customers.

CMS signed approximately 110 MW of new load contracts year-to-date in Q1 2026, already exceeding the roughly 100 MW signed in all of 2025, on top of approximately 450 MW connected last year, supporting 2%-3% annual sales growth guidance.

The Michigan Potash & Salt contract represents roughly 130 jobs and over $1.3 billion of investment in Michigan, while the broader economic development pipeline remains around 9 GW with about 15% (over 1 GW) from non-data center opportunities.

Rate relief net of investments drove +$0.11/share in Q1, partially offset by a -$0.05/share storm impact from a sizable March ice storm; year-to-go guidance assumes -$0.23/share from normal weather, +$0.24/share from regulatory items, +$0.04/share from lower O&M, and +$0.06-$0.13/share from NorthStar net of parent financing costs.

CMS executed approximately $495 million of equity forward contracts in Q1 (settling ~$142 million), substantially derisking the planned ~$700 million 2026 equity issuance, with average annual equity needs of ~$750 million over the next four years, front-end loaded.

Moody's and Fitch reaffirmed CMS's credit ratings in March, but Moody's moved the utility to a negative outlook due to the size of the 5-year capital plan relative to cost recovery timing, prompting management to evaluate countermeasures including potential rate-making capital structure and cost of capital actions.
Full year adjusted EBITDA loss was $31 million, a $113 million or 79% improvement versus 2024.
Q4 adjusted EBITDA loss was $4 million, an 84% or $23 million improvement versus Q4 2024.
Revenue declined 10% year-over-year in Q4 (6% excluding discontinued Canada operations), while gross margin improved 160 basis points to 24.6%.
Full year gross margin improved by 390 basis points to 24.7%, and the company is targeting advancement toward 25% in 2026.
The company ended the quarter with cash, restricted cash, and inventory of $207 million, with full year cash used in operating activities improving by more than $118 million or 67% year-over-year.

The company expects to close the Kirkland's acquisition on or around April 1, with the combined omnichannel Pillar 1 approximating $1.5 billion in annualized revenue plus an additional $500 million from another transaction agreed to in principle.

Three large pillar acquisitions (one per pillar) are in progress, which collectively could add north of $1.5 billion in additional revenue, potentially bringing the annualized run rate to approximately $3 billion.
For Q1 2026, the company expects 3% to 5% revenue growth and approximately 30% year-over-year EBITDA improvement, with a stretch goal of reaching profitability by Q4 2026.
The company is targeting low- to mid-single-digit e-commerce revenue growth for full year 2026, with positive year-over-year growth already observed from January through late February.

Management believes consolidated gross margins can expand above 30% within 36 months as Pillar 2 (financial services, margins north of 50%) and Pillar 3 (home services, margins in excess of 40%) scale alongside the core retail business.
